claims.statement: Notebook integration tests execute the normal notebook code through Jupytext and Papermill with parameter reductions, while the launcher removes the legacy TEST and QUICK_TEST variables so test-only branches are not enabled.
The override validation checks that override keys name real notebooks and that every declared parameter is visible to Papermill and remains reachable on both preview and canonical injection paths.

Chapter tests discover notebook-like Python sources from numbered chapter directories and dataset cards, while case-study tests discover numbered stages, expand multi-invocation entries into separate pytest cases, and retain stage-major ordering.

The notebook runner converts source to a temporary notebook, executes into a transient output notebook with per-cell saves and progress logging, reports the failing Papermill cell, restores the process environment, and removes temporary notebooks and kernelspecs.

The notebook harness isolates writes in a session- or xdist-worker-specific ML4T_OUTPUT_DIR and supplies a checkout-shaped ML4T_RELEASE_ROOT without production run logs, preventing local published registries from participating in canonical reads or being mutated.

Raw reduced data is resolved separately from precomputed intermediates; session setup replaces seeded artifact subdirectories, copies chapter and case-study intermediates, reconciles legacy prediction columns, and then seeds only additional result gaps.

Reduced raw fixtures enforce producer ownership: production-derived Dataset declarations and the synthetic microstructure generator must not overlap, and fixture files without a declared producer are limited to an explicit shrinking ratchet.
The raw fixture manifest is checked bidirectionally against builder declarations and disk contents, including declared entity counts and important timestamp representations.

Fixture registry maintenance treats pinned artifact bytes as authoritative: training rows whose feature or label digests are absent are stale and are deleted leaf-first together with dependent predictions, metrics, populations, and backtests.

Registry sampling rejects destinations that resolve into a case-study production tree, preserves rows backed by shipped prediction artifacts across resampling, and samples complete downstream backtest structures rather than arbitrary isolated rows.

Notebook skips can carry machine-checkable fixture or registry blockers; once a decidable blocker disappears, honoured_skip_reason stops applying the skip, while an unavailable fixture is not misread as evidence that the blocker expired.

Case-study notebook cases normally run independently against seeded intermediates, but a stage may declare requires_stage when it needs preview-tier rows produced in the same workspace; focused or sharded runs then skip with the missing prerequisite named.
Pytest appends each completed test or setup skip to a flushed JSONL results file so partial results survive process termination.

The primary CI workflow uses path filtering to build incremental chapter and case-study matrices for pull requests, but shared changes and pushes to main, schedules, post-image runs, or manual run_all requests expand to the full shipped matrix.

Normal notebook lanes execute in the resolved ml4t image, special Python 3.12 notebooks run from an explicit list in ml4t-py312, and Neo4j notebooks run in dependency order against a service container.
When image inputs change, notebook CI resolves a candidate image from the same commit and checks its installed distributions against uv.lock before execution.

Data-dependent required CI jobs gate fixture checkout and notebook execution at the step level when a fork lacks the deploy key, preserving a satisfiable check context while explicitly reporting that no data-dependent assertion ran.
The manual full-test workflow supports all, chapters-only, and case-studies-only scopes and ends with an aggregate summary that fails when any required lane fails.

Paired case-study notebooks must set Jupytext cell_metadata_filter to tags,-all and must not carry inline Papermill metadata, preventing execution metadata from desynchronizing the committed Python and ipynb pair.

The SQLite notebook catalog and single-notebook worker form a managed campaign path separate from ordinary parametrized pytest: the catalog inventories and classifies notebooks, and the worker can execute either reduced mode through run_notebook or full mode without reductions.

The required `test-unit` job runs `pytest tests/` by subtraction against `.github/ci/unit-test-quarantine.txt`, so the Chapter 13 sequence-window, live ETF macro-availability, and backtest-runner helper regressions run in the fast gate without separate workflow enumeration because none is quarantined.

Chapter 13's canonical plain and patched sequence builders include the target-dated decision row as the final row of each feature window, retain the earliest full window and an exact-lookback symbol as one sample, and are regression-tested to cover equivalent rows and targets; this contract does not apply to forecast contexts intentionally ending before their forecast path.

The live ETF regime feature path shifts yield-curve timestamps by the case-study's configured availability lag before a backward as-of join to trading sessions, then computes the configured session-based z-score; its regression test proves full-data results equal results from macro inputs truncated to what was available by the previous day and pins the live lag and threshold to the case-study configuration.

The vectorized backtest path refuses an aggregate gross period return below -100% before risk overlays because `sum(weight * y_true)` has no broker or intraperiod liquidation state, while regression coverage confirms a bounded, fully invested long loss above -100% remains allowed and an unbrokered short loss below -100% raises with contributing-position diagnostics.

The prose-numeral guard scans paired percent-format Jupytext Python sources, ignores markdown cells tagged `results`, and runs a self-test that proves both the exemption and the corresponding untagged failure before CI scans the repository.

The prose-numeral guard is a lexical ratchet rather than semantic prose analysis: it detects a deliberately narrow set of decimals and percentages while masking other literal contexts, rejects new or increased sites, and requires stale allowlist counts to be reduced on whole-repository runs.
